name: Dicalcium phosphate; low-temperature endothermic process; at processing plant
description: This unit process is a cradle-to-gate dataset of production of 1 kg  dicalcium phosphate in the US.

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Represents production at the national level.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: The process is based on the chemical reactants required to produce dicalcium phosphate (phosphoric acid and quicklime). The reaction equation  H3PO4+CaO -> CaHPO4 + H2O was used to calculate quantities of phosphoric acid and quicklime needed to produce 1 kg of dicalcium phosphate.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Life cycle inventory was originally assembled using the SimaPro software platform (Version 8.0.4.26) and was modified for submission using the OpenLCA platform (Version 1.3.0).
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Energy requirements were modeled using literature sources (M. Gollinger, Z. Kowalski, Environmental and Economic Assessment of Feed Phosphate Technology Modernization). Water and land use are not included.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Only material inputs were accounted for.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Some feed ingredient minerals and vitamins were not availabe in US-EI database. In this case the unavailable chemical was created using the calculated mass of each reactant necessary to produce one kilogram of product. The stoichiometric equation (H3PO4+CaO -> CaHPO4 + H2O) was obtained from literature data. Moles were converted from the reaction equation to mass (kg).  The electricity and natural gas requirements were taken from literature data.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Energy input data for low-temperature endothermic process  was addopted directly from the literature. Water requirements for this chemical compound  are a data gap, but small inclusion rates in pig diets suggests it is reasonable to exclude.

sources.name: Development of Life Cycle Inventory data for U.S. Swine Production Scenarios

reviews.details: University of Arkansas swine dataset mapped to USLCI technosphere flows and FEDEFL elementary flows for publication on the Federal LCA Commons. Review covers mapping crosswalks, cutoff flows, and export structure.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: These data may be used in Situation C2, “Accounting without interactions.”  This is applicable to accounting studies that according to their goal definition do not include any interaction with other systems.
